title: Global Commodity Manager (Senior Advisor) at Dell Technologies Sees Asia Vital Components as a Strong Partner for Custom AI-Server Cold Plates
expert: Global Commodity Manager (Senior Advisor) at Dell Technologies; managed the AVC account for three years and made cold-plate price awards
verdict: The expert, who awarded Dell's cold-plate business, saw reference cold-plate prices fall 40–50% as GB volumes scaled while custom ASIC cooling carries a ~40% premium and the first qualified supplier takes up to 100% of launch volume.

Nvidia content and share: 🟢 Up to 100% of launch volume to the first qualified supplier, then 50/50 (his allocation rule), consistent with JPM's ~50% per project (SB #58861).
ASIC liquid-cooling start: 🟢 Custom ASIC cooling content ~40% above reference designs (first-hand), first read. → Tenet 2 (ASIC >50% of liquid revenue) ↑
🟢 At least 80% of the custom ASIC servers he sourced were liquid-cooled (estimate).
Gross margin: 🔴 Reference cold-plate prices down 40–50% as GB200/GB300 volume scaled (first-hand) vs JPM's ASP raises on switch trays (SB #58857): conflicting. → Tenet 3 (GM 34%+) ↓
🔴 2–3% (up to 5%) quarterly cost-down targets; copper is 30–40% of cost.

changes: Reference cold-plate prices -40-50% (first-hand) vs JPM: AVC raised ASPs on Nvidia/Mellanox switch-tray cold plates (SB #58857): conflicting (different products).
Launch allocation 100% then 50/50 vs JPM ~50% share in each AI project (SB #58861): consistent.
First read on AVC field quality: leak incidents below 1% of units; no earlier expert call or stored row.
thesis_impact: Tenet 1 (Rubin content and share): → — dual sourcing drives toward 50/50 once a second source qualifies.
Tenet 2 (ASIC >50% of liquid revenue): ↑ — at least 80% of custom ASIC servers liquid-cooled; content ~40% above reference.
Tenet 3 (GM 34%+): ↓ — reference prices -40-50% and 2-3% quarterly cost-downs; copper 30-40% of cost.
